subject.title: [Bug]: --to flag ignored when using --agent with custom channel, all sessions map to main

question: Should the active fix for explicit `openclaw agent --agent --channel --to` routing use bounded or opaque recipient-derived session keys with upgrade handling, or may it persist raw recipient-derived keys and intentionally fork existing main-session continuity?
rationale: The source-level bug is valid, but the remaining implementation choice changes persisted session identity and can expose recipient identifiers, so automation should not choose the permanent key/privacy contract alone.

options.title: Refresh With Bounded/Opaque Keys
options.body: Refresh or replace the open PR on current main, preserve explicit `--session-key` and `--session-id` precedence, and use a bounded or maintainer-approved opaque recipient-key contract with upgrade behavior addressed.

options.title: Accept Raw Recipient Keys
options.body: Land raw channel/recipient-derived keys only after the PR body and tests make that persisted identifier contract and continuity break explicit.

options.title: Pause For Design
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose a different compatibility or privacy design before implementation continues.

recommendation.title: Refresh With Bounded/Opaque Keys
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open PR on current main, preserve explicit `--session-key` and `--session-id` precedence, and use a bounded or maintainer-approved opaque recipient-key contract with upgrade behavior addressed.
